gradients.name: brand-gradient
gradients.purpose: "Request a free call" buttons and the favicon tile only. The indigo radials behind the opening and the demo stage, their grids and the teal glow are fields, not this gradient.

display.purpose: The opening statement only; serif 500, white, closing phrase held on one line above 480px.

headline.purpose: Section H2s (including the call heading) and the closing-band H2; serif.

index.purpose: Service names in the practice index; serif.

title.purpose: Route H3s in the routes panel; Public Sans bold.

body-large.purpose: The call section sub-line, ink-500, max 34ch.

body.purpose: Running text, tabular numerals. Case rows: input 0.9375rem, result 600 1.0625rem.

label.purpose: Geist Mono uppercase teal: duration tags beside or beneath their title, and the one diagram boundary label (0.6875rem). Never above a heading, leading a row, or as interface chrome.

shadows.name: shadow-1
shadows.purpose: Resting: the routes panel and primary buttons. Keeps its indigo tint in dark mode.

shadows.name: shadow-2
shadows.purpose: Raised: the form panel at rest (the one action), button hover, and under the sent-state halo.

shadows.name: card-on-stage
shadows.purpose: Demo app cards on the dark stage only.

shadows.name: focus-halo
shadows.purpose: Input focus and form-panel sent state.

motion.name: panel-sent
motion.purpose: Form panel border, halo and Raised shadow on success.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: Confirmation line fades up 4px. All motion off under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: demo-read
motion.purpose: The source is read top to bottom; each mark lights (260ms ease-out) in turn. No scan line.

motion.name: demo-swap
motion.purpose: Scene change: the two app frames stay put; only their contents cross-fade.

motion.name: demo-chip
motion.purpose: Chips travel one at a time on a shallow arc and settle exactly on the field value line.

motion.name: demo-land
motion.purpose: A field value fades in on a Teal Tint flash; computed fields land the same way without a chip.

motion.name: demo-step
motion.purpose: Step label fades up 4px on change; status text uses 320ms.

motion.name: demo-hold
motion.purpose: Each scene runs exactly 7600ms; the finished record holds for whatever remains (at least 1600ms). Tab progress fills over the same 7600ms.

motion.name: demo-breathe
motion.purpose: Working status dot pulses to 35% opacity until the scene settles.

motion.name: demo-sequencing
motion.purpose: Steps are sequenced with timers, never on animation completion, so a throttled browser cannot stall the loop.

motion.name: case-color
motion.purpose: Case row text color on hover and when it starts playing; its 2px teal line grows over the 7.6s scene.

motion.name: object-turn
motion.value: continuous: spin 0.14 rad/s about its own axis; lean wobble at 0.27 and 0.19 rad/s; float at 0.55 rad/s
motion.purpose: The opening object turns slowly; the twist carries the highlights round the loop.

motion.name: object-tilt
motion.value: pointer-follow, eased 5% per frame, up to ~0.18 / 0.28 rad
motion.purpose: The object leans a few degrees toward the pointer; returns to rest on pointer leave.

motion.name: object-reveal
motion.purpose: The canvas fades in on its first rendered frame. Off screen or hidden: paused. Reduced motion: one still pose.

heroTreatment.source: tracelet-vendor/pages/css/tracelet-landing.css (hero grid, 54px); layout on the Metalab model (chosen 2026-10-04)
heroTreatment.field: radial-gradient(120% 90% at 75% 40%, #19207a 0%, #0f1556 45%, #080c33 100%), same in both modes
heroTreatment.grid: linear-gradient(rgba(255,255,255,0.055) 1px, transparent 1px), linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(255,255,255,0.055) 1px, transparent 1px); background-size 54px 54px; mask radial-gradient(110% 95% at 85% 0%, #000 25%, transparent 72%)
heroTreatment.glow: radial-gradient(closest-side, rgba(0, 118, 163, 0.35), transparent), blur(30px), bottom right

object.renderer: seafin-site/hero3d.js, three.js 0.170 via jsDelivr import map, WebGL, DPR capped at 1.75, ACES tone mapping, RoomEnvironment
object.form: ribbon ring, stadium section (half-width 0.62, half-thickness and edge radius 0.17, ring radius 1.55), one full twist per lap
object.material: MeshPhysicalMaterial #151b6e, metalness 0.55, roughness 0.17, clearcoat 1, clearcoatRoughness 0.05, envMapIntensity 1.5
object.lights: teal rim #38b3da (6), violet rim #7d86ff (4), white key (0.7)
object.framing: canvas >= 900px wide: large, partly cropped, right of the statement; narrower: above it
object.fallback: no WebGL or module failure: the indigo field stays

heroTreatment.minHeight: clamp(560px, calc(100svh - 64px), 880px); content anchored to the bottom

narrative.overview:
Seafin does not have its own visual world. By the user's standing pin (PRODUCT.md, Brand Commitments), Seafin's site uses the Wardix design system: `tracelet` repo `design.md` on `origin/dev` ("Vigilant Infrastructure") for doctrine, and `tracelet-vendor/pages/css/tracelet-landing.css` for token values. This file records how that system landed on Seafin, and where Seafin departs from the Wardix marketing site. When this file is silent, the upstream `design.md` governs; when they disagree, this file records what Seafin shipped.

The page is built on the Metalab model (chosen 2026-10-04 after a study of leading design studios): the opening is one big serif statement and one crafted object on the Wardix dark field (deep indigo under the fading engineering grid and a soft teal glow), with nothing else on the first screen. Below it the page runs white with hairline rules, one Canvas band and a Bastion close: the form in its own section, the practice index, a played demo of real-world builds, and where the work runs. Serif headings, sans everything else, one gradient button. Restraint carries the premium feel; the two crafted pieces (the opening object and the build demo) carry the craft. It reads as a consulting practice's page, not a person's or a product's.

Seafin departs from the Wardix marketing site in four places, each on purpose. There are no mono labels above headings, because Impeccable's craft floor bans them. There is no photography or raster imagery: no scenic hero (it would make Seafin read as a copy of the Wardix site), no founder portrait, no product screenshot. The pictures are made, not shot: one rendered 3D object in the opening, the demo's mock app cards (four scenes modelled on published small-business cases), and drawn teal route diagrams. The brand gradient is narrowed to the single primary action. And only two things move on their own, each in its own section.
keyCharacteristics: A deep indigo opening holding one serif statement and one glossy 3D object, then a white page with one Canvas band and a Bastion close; dark mode from the same token pairs, with light surfaces pinned light.
Source Serif 4 for the statement, the section headings and the service names; Public Sans for everything readable; Geist Mono only for short functional tags.
One radius family: 6 / 10 / 14 / 26, plus 4px for inline highlights.
One action per page, one label for it, one gradient on it.
Two self-moving pieces (the opening object, the build demo), everything else still; no photography; no invented proof.

rules.name: The One Gradient Rule
rules.body: The indigo-to-teal brand gradient appears only on "Request a free call" buttons (nav, opening, form submit, closing band) and on the favicon tile. Not on text, cards, section backgrounds, or a second button. The tonal indigo radials behind the opening and the demo stage, their grid lines and the teal glow are fields, not the brand gradient, and appear nowhere else.

rules.name: The Dark Grounds Rule
rules.body: Deep Indigo is for the opening field and the demo stage; Bastion Navy is for the closing band. They never swap, and no other surface goes dark.

rules.name: The Status-Means-State Rule
rules.body: Green, gold and red mean real system state. Seafin uses only red, and only for a failed form send. The demo's status dot is teal, never green.

rules.name: The Serif-Is-For-The-Page Rule
rules.body: Serif is for the opening statement, section H2s, the closing H2 and the service names in the practice index, which act as the headings of what Seafin sells. Panel titles and everything inside the demo are Public Sans.

rules.name: The Mono-Tags-Never-Lead Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono uppercase labels are short and functional: duration tags set beside their title (desktop) or beneath it (≤960px), and the one label that names a drawn boundary in a diagram. A mono label never sits above a heading, never leads a row, and never stands in for interface chrome.

rules.name: The Quiet Elevation Rule
rules.body: Nothing at rest sits above Resting except the form panel (the one action) and the demo stage (the one showcase), which rest on Raised. Overlay is for overlays. The deep Card on Stage shadow exists only on a dark ground, where a light shadow would vanish.

dos: Do take every token from the Wardix set (upstream `design.md` + `tracelet-landing.css`) and add a Seafin-local token only when the build needs it (as with `line-strong`, `danger`).
Do reserve the brand gradient for "Request a free call" buttons, and use that same label everywhere the action appears.
Do open with one serif statement, one lede line, one button and one crafted object on the deep indigo field with the 54px grid; nothing else on the first screen.
Do use Source Serif 4 for the statement, section headings and practice-index service names only, and Public Sans for panel titles and everything inside a mock interface.
Do use Geist Mono uppercase only for short functional tags beside or beneath their title, or to name a drawn boundary.

Do give every looping animation a shared rhythm, keep its frames fixed so nothing shifts as content lands, pause it off screen and in hidden tabs, and make its markup a composed still frame for reduced motion and no-JS.
Do pin light surfaces (the form panel, demo cards) to the light tokens when they sit on a dark ground or in dark mode.
Do list services and cases as open ruled rows, and put a two-option comparison in one 14px panel, rather than a grid of cards.
donts: Don't place an uppercase mono label, kicker or eyebrow above a heading or at the head of a row, or use mono as interface chrome (the Wardix marketing site's `.eyebrow` pattern is not carried over).
Don't add photography or raster imagery to the consulting page: no scenic photos, no founder portrait, no product screenshots.
Don't add a second 3D object or a third self-moving piece; anything else stays still until the visitor acts.
Don't put icons in tiles, circles or filled badges, or use emoji icons.
Don't use Card on Stage off a dark ground, or Overlay on anything at rest.
Don't add prose explaining the page to the visitor, section intros, decorative bold, or decorative numbers.

Don't show invented proof: no hypothetical case studies, logos, testimonials or counts. Demo scenes may be modelled on published cases, but their data stays illustrative and the source businesses are never named or framed as clients or results.
Don't use pills, radii outside 4 / 6 / 10 / 14 / 26, or sharp cards.
